en: In the miracle as an action, a connection of cause and effect is given to the understanding, and the domain of its concepts is acknowledged; but at the same time its domain is thereby destroyed, in that the cause is not something as determinate as the effect, but is supposed to be an infinite; since the connection of cause and effect in the understanding is the equality of determinateness, their opposition only this, that in the one this determinateness is activity, in the other passivity, — here [but] an infinite, with infinite activity, is at the same time supposed to have, in the action itself, a most limited effect.
Not the sublation of the domain of the understanding, but that it is at the same time posited and sublated, is what is unnatural.
Just as, on the one hand, the positing of an infinite cause contradicts the positing of a finite effect, so too the infinite sublates the determinate effect.

There, viewed from the standpoint of the understanding, the infinite is only a negative, the indeterminate, to which something determinate is attached; here, from the side of the infinite as something existing, it is a spirit that acts, and the determinateness of the effect of a spirit is its negative side; only from another standpoint, in comparison, can its action appear determinate; in itself, according to its being, it is the sublation of a determinateness and in itself infinite.
zh: 在作为行动的奇迹里，知性得到了一个原因与结果的关联，它那些概念的地盘也被承认了；但这样一来它的地盘同时又被毁掉了，因为原因并不是像结果那样确定的东西，而应该是一个无限者；既然在知性里原因与结果的关联就是规定性的相等，它们的对立只在于：在其中一个里这种规定性是活动，在另一个里是被动，——而这里[却]要同时在行动本身中让一个带有无限活动的无限者产生一个极其有限的结果。
不自然的地方并不是知性的地盘被扬弃，而是它同时被设定又被扬弃。
正如一方面设定一个无限的原因与设定一个有限的结果相矛盾，同样，无限者也扬弃了确定的结果。
在那里，从知性的观点看，无限者只是一个否定者、一个无规定者，一个确定的东西被挂到它上面；而在这里，从作为存在者的无限者这一面看，它是一个起作用的精神，而一个精神的作用的规定性就是它否定的一面；只有在比较中从另一个观点出发，它的行动才能显得是确定的；而就其自身、就其存在来说，它是扬弃一种规定性，并且在自身中是无限的。

en: When a god acts, it is only from spirit to spirit; efficacy presupposes an object on which it acts; but the effect of the spirit is the sublation of that object.

The going-forth of the divine is only a development, namely that it, in sublating the opposed, presents itself in the union; but in miracles the spirit appears as acting on bodies — the cause would then not be a formed spirit whose form, considered merely in its opposition, could as body enter, equal to another and capable of being opposed to it, into the connection of cause and effect; this connection would be a community of the spirit, which is spirit only insofar as it has nothing in common with the body, and of the body, which is body because it has nothing in common with the spirit — but spirit and body have nothing in common; they are absolutely opposed.

Their union, in which their opposition ceases, is a life, i.e. formed spirit; and if this acts as something divine, undivided, then its doing is a marriage with a kindred essence, with something divine, and a begetting, a development of something new, of the presentation of their union; but insofar as the spirit acts in another, opposed form, as something hostile, dominating, it has forgotten its divinity.

Miracles are therefore the presentation of the most ungodly, because they are the most unnatural and contain, bound together, the harshest opposition of spirit and body in all its monstrous coarseness.
Divine doing is the restoration and presentation of oneness; miracle, the highest tearing-apart.

The expectation that has been stirred up — to raise, through wonderful activities of this actual one, the actuality associated with the transfigured Jesus exalted to a god, to divinity — is therefore so far from being fulfilled that it rather increases all the more the harshness of this adjunction of an actual thing.

But it is so much greater for [us] than for the members of the first Christian congregation, by as much as we have more understanding than they, who, touched by the Oriental spirit, had carried out the separation of spirit and body less completely and had delivered less to the understanding as objects.
Where we cognize determinate actuality, historical objectivity, with the understanding, there is often spirit for them; and where we posit only pure spirit, there it is still embodied for them.

Of the latter kind of view, the form in which they grasp what we call immortality, namely the immortality of the soul, is an example; it appears to them as a resurrection of the body; both views are the extremes within the Greek spirit; the former the extreme of reason, which opposes a soul, a negative against all understanding, and its object, the dead body; the latter the extreme, so to speak, of a positive capacity of reason, which posits the body as living, while it at the same time assumed it to be dead; whereas for the Greeks body and soul remain in a living form, in the two extremes, by contrast, death is a separation of body and soul, and in the one the body is nothing more for the soul, in the other the body is something persisting even without life.

In other things, where we cognize only with the understanding, and something actual — or, which amounts to the same, some foreign spirit — the first Christians mix in their own spirit. — In the writings of the Jews we see past histories, individual situations and the past spirit of men; in the Jewish acts of worship, commanded action whose spirit, purpose and thoughts no longer exist for us, no longer have any truth; for them all this still had truth and spirit — but their truth, their spirit; they did not let it become objective.

The spirit that they give to passages of the prophets and of other Jewish books is, in their sense, neither — with regard to the prophets — the opinion of finding predictions of actualities in them, nor, on their side, the application to actuality.

It is an uncertain, formless hovering between actuality and spirit; on the one hand only the spirit is considered in the actuality, on the other hand the actuality itself as such is present, but not fixed.

To cite an example: John (12, 14 ff.) refers to the circumstance that Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey an expression of the prophet, whose inspiration saw such a procession, and John lets it find its truth in the procession of Jesus.

The proofs that similar passages of the Jewish books are in part cited incorrectly in themselves, against the literal sense of the original text, in part explained against their sense, which they receive through their context, in part refer to quite different actualities, to circumstances and men contemporary with the prophets, in part are only isolated inspiration of the prophets — all these proofs hit only the actuality of the relation that the apostles set up between them and the life-circumstances of Jesus, not its truth and spirit; just as little is its truth visible in the strict objective assumption that the real words and visions of the prophets are the earlier expression of later actualities.

The spirit of the relation that the friends of Christ find between the visions of the prophets and the events of Jesus would be grasped too weakly if it were placed merely in the comparison of similarity of situations, in a comparison such as when we often add to the presentation of a situation the precise expression of old writers.

In the example cited above, John says expressly that the friends of Jesus recognized these relations only after Jesus had been transfigured, after the spirit had come upon them; had John seen in this relation a mere notion, a mere similarity of different things, this remark would not have been needed; but as it is, in the spirit, that vision of the prophet and this circumstance in an action of Jesus are one; and since the relation is only in the spirit, the objective view of it as a coincidence of actual, of individual things falls away.
This spirit, which fixes the actual as little as it turns it into something indeterminate, and cognizes in it nothing individual but something spiritual, is especially also Joh.

11, 51 visible, where John, with regard to the maxim of Caiaphas and its application, that it is better that one man die for the people than that the whole come into danger, reminds us that Caiaphas did not speak this for himself as an individual, but as high priest in prophetic inspiration (πϱοεϕήτευσεν).

What we would perhaps regard from the standpoint of an instrument of divine providence, in that John saw something filled by the spirit, since the character of the view of Jesus and his friends could be nothing so opposed as to the standpoint of taking everything as machine, tool, instrument, but was rather the highest faith in spirit; and where one glimpses a unity in the coincidence of actions which, taken singly for themselves, lack this unity, the intention of the whole of the effect, and regards these actions (like those of Caiaphas) as subject to it, governed and guided by it without consciousness in their relation to the unity, as actualities and instruments, there John sees unity of the spirit and, in this action itself, the spirit of the whole effect acting; he speaks of Caiaphas as himself filled with the spirit in which the necessity of the fate of Jesus lay.
zh: 一个神起作用时，只是从精神到精神；起作用总要预设一个被作用的对象；但精神的作用就是扬弃这个对象。

神圣者的走出只是一种发展，即它扬弃了对立者，从而在结合中展示自己；但在奇迹里，精神显得是在作用于物体，这样一来原因就不会是一个有形态的精神了——这种形态如果只在它的对立中来看，就可以作为物体，作为一个与另一个相等、并且能与它相对的东西，进入原因和结果的关联；这种关联就会是精神与物体的共同性：精神之所以是精神，只因为它与物体毫无共同之处；物体之所以是物体，只因为它与精神毫无共同之处，——可精神与物体毫无共同之处；它们是绝对对立的。
它们的结合——在这种结合中它们的对立停止了——是一种生命，即有形态的精神；如果这个精神作为神圣的、未被分开的东西起作用，那么它的作为就是与同类的本质、与神圣者的婚配，是生育、发展出新的东西，即展示它们的结合；但如果精神以另一种对立的形态，作为敌对的东西、统治的东西起作用，那它就忘记了自己的神性。
所以奇迹是最不神圣的东西的展示，因为奇迹是最不自然的，并且把精神和物体最坚硬的对立连同它全部骇人的粗野一起联结在内。
神圣的作为是重建和展示一体；奇迹则是最高程度的撕裂。
于是，那种被激发起来的期待——想通过这个现实者的神奇活动，把与得了荣耀、被提升为神的耶稣结为同伴的现实性提升为神性——非但完全没有得到满足，反而更加重了这种附加一个现实者的生硬。
不过它对我们来说，比对这些最早的基督教教团的成员来说要大得多，因为我们比他们有更多的知性，而他们受东方精神的吹拂，精神和物体的分离完成得较少，交给知性当作对象的东西也较少。
凡是我们用知性认识确定的现实性、历史客观性的地方，在他们那里往往还是精神；而凡是我们只设定纯粹精神的地方，在他们那里它仍然是具有肉身的。

后一种看法的一个例子，就是他们用来把握我们所说的不死、即灵魂不死的那种形式；在他们看来，它显现为肉体的复活；这两种看法是希腊精神之内的两个极端；前者是理性的极端，它把灵魂——一个反对一切知性的否定者——和知性的对象、即死去的肉体对立起来；后者可以说是理性的另一种积极能力的极端，这种能力把肉体设定为活着的，同时又把它当成死的；而在希腊人那里，肉体和灵魂还停留在一种活生生的形态里，在这两个极端里则相反，死亡是肉体和灵魂的分离，在一个极端里肉体对灵魂来说什么也不是了，在另一个极端里肉体即使没有生命也仍然留存。

在另一些事情上，我们只用知性去认识，认识的是现实的东西——或者说，这等于说，是某种陌生的精神——，最早的基督徒就把自己的精神掺了进去。——在犹太人的著作里，我们看到的是过去的历史、个别的处境和人们曾经有过的精神；在犹太人的礼拜仪式里，我们看到的是被命令去做的行为，它的精神、目的和思想对我们来说已经不存在了，再也没有真理；而对他们来说，这一切还有真理、还有精神，但那是他们自己的真理、他们自己的精神，他们不让它成为客观的。
他们赋予先知书和其他犹太书卷某些段落的那个精神，在他们的理解里，既不是——就先知而言——想在其中找到对现实性的预言的看法，也不是他们这一方面对现实性的应用。
这是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的、没有形态的飘浮；一方面，在现实性里被考察的只是精神，另一方面，现实性本身作为现实性是存在的，但并没有被固定下来。
举一个例子：约翰（12, 14 及以下）把先知的一句话联系到耶稣骑着驴进入耶路撒冷这件事上——那位先知的灵感看见了这样一支队伍，而约翰则让这句话在耶稣的这支队伍里找到自己的真理。

那些证明——说犹太书卷里类似的段落，有的本身就违背原文字面意思而被引用错了，有的则被解释得违背了它们通过上下文才获得的意思，有的指的是完全另外一些现实性、与先知同时的处境和人，有的只是先知孤立的灵感——所有这些证明只触及使徒在它们和耶稣的生活处境之间建立的那种关系的现实性，触及不到它的真理和精神；同样，在那种严格的客观假设里——即先知真正说过的话和所见的异象是后来现实性的较早表达——它的真理也看不见。
基督的朋友们在先知的异象和耶稣的事件之间找到的那种关系，它的精神如果只被放在对诸处境相似性的比较里，被放在这样一种比较里——就像我们常常给对某个处境的描述添上古代作家的确切说法——那就把握得太弱了。
在上面所举的例子那里，约翰明确地说，耶稣的朋友们是在耶稣得了荣耀之后、在精神降临到他们身上之后，才认识到这些关系的；假如约翰在这种关系里看到的只是一种突发的念头、一种不同东西的单纯相似，那就不需要这句说明了；但事情却是这样：在精神里，先知的那个异象和耶稣某个行动中的这个情况是同一回事；而既然这种关系只在精神里，那么把它当作现实东西、个别东西的巧合的那种客观看法就落空了。
这种精神，它同样不去固定现实的东西，或者说把它变成无规定的东西，并且在其中认识到的不是个别的东西，而是精神性的东西，它尤其还见于 Joh.
11, 51 看得见，在那里，约翰就该亚法的准则以及对这准则的应用——一个人替民众死，总比整个民族陷于危险要好——提醒说，该亚法这话并不是作为个人为自己说的，而是作为大祭司在预言的灵感中说的（πϱοεϕήτευσεν）。

我们会从神的护佑的一件工具这个观点去看的东西，约翰在其中看到的却是被精神充满的东西，因为耶稣和他的朋友们的看法，其品格不可能有比这更与那种把一切都当作机器、工具、器具的观点相对立的了，它毋宁是对精神的最高信仰；而在人们看到许多行动巧合中的统一——这些行动单独来看缺少这种统一、缺少整个作用的意图——并且把这些行动（如该亚法的行动）看作隶属于这种统一、在它们与统一的关系中被这种统一无意识地统治和引导、把它们当作现实性和工具的地方，约翰看到的却是精神的统一，并且看到整个作用的精神就在这个行动本身中起作用；他说该亚法自己就被那精神所充满，而耶稣命运中的必然性就在这精神里。

en: Thus too, seen with the soul of the apostles, the miracles lose the harshness that the opposition of spirit and body in them has for us, since it is evident that those men lacked the European understanding, which so strips all spirit from whatever comes into consciousness and fixes it into absolute objectivities, into actualities absolutely opposed to spirit, that their cognition is rather an indeterminate hovering between actuality and spirit, which indeed still separated the two, but did not separate them so irrevocably, and moreover did not merge into pure nature, but already gave the clear opposition itself, which with greater development had to become a pairing of the living and the dead, of the divine and the actual, which through the placing of the actual Jesus alongside the transfigured, the become-God, showed satisfaction to the deepest drive after religion, but did not grant it, and made it into an infinite, inextinguishable and unappeased longing; for the longing, in its highest enthusiasm, in the raptures of the most finely organized souls breathing the highest love, always faces the individual, something objective, personal, after union with which all the depths of their beautiful feelings languished, but which union, because it is an individual, is eternally impossible, since it always remains over against them, eternally in their consciousness, and never lets religion become complete life.
zh: 所以，用使徒们的灵魂来看，奇迹也就失去了精神和物体的对立在奇迹里对我们所具有的那种生硬，因为很明显，他们缺少欧洲式的知性——这种知性把一切进入意识的东西的精神都抽掉，把它固定为绝对的对象性、固定为与精神绝对对立的现实性——以至于他们的认识毋宁是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的飘浮，这种飘浮虽然还把两者分开，却没有分得那么不可挽回，而且终究没有汇入纯粹的自然，反而已经给出了那种清晰的对立，这种对立在进一步发展中必定会成为一种配对：活的东西和死的东西、神圣的东西和现实的东西的配对，它由于把现实的耶稣与得了荣耀的、变成神的耶稣并列，而向最深的宗教冲动显示出满足，却没有给予满足，反而把它变成一种无限的、不可磨灭的、无法平息的渴望；因为这种渴望在它最高的狂热里、在最精细地组织起来、呼出最高爱的灵魂的迷醉里，面对的总是那个个体，一个客观的、人格的东西，它们美好感受的一切深处都渴望着与它结合，但这种结合——因为它是一个个体——永远不可能，因为它始终与它们相对，永远留在它们的意识里，使宗教永远不能成为完整的生命。

en: In all forms of the Christian religion that have developed in the ongoing fate of time, this basic character of opposition rests in the divine, which is supposed to be present only in consciousness, never in life — from the rapturous unions of the enthusiast, who renounces all manifoldness of life, even the purest, in which the spirit enjoys itself, and is conscious only of God, and thus could remove the opposition of personality only in death, to the actuality of the most manifold consciousness, of union with the fate of the world and of God's opposition to it — either the felt opposition in all actions and expressions of life, which purchase their legitimacy through the feeling of the servitude and nullity of their opposition, as in the Catholic church, or God's opposition in merely more or less devout thoughts, as in the Protestant church — either the opposition of a hating God to life, as a disgrace and a crime, in some sects of the same, or of a kind one to life and its joys, as all received, benefits and gifts from him, as all actuality, into which then also the form of spirit hovering over it is drawn down to historical objective view in the idea of a divine man, of the prophets, etc. —: between these extremes of the manifold or diminished consciousness of friendship, of hatred or of indifference toward the world, between these extremes, which lie within the opposition of God and the world, of the divine and of life, the Christian church has run the circle forwards and backwards, but it is against its essential character to find rest in an impersonal living beauty; and it is its fate that church and state, divine service and life, piety and virtue, spiritual and worldly doing can never melt into one.
zh: 在基督教的一切形态里——这些形态是在时间不断展开的命运中发展出来的——对立的这个基本特征都落在神圣者之中，这神圣者只应存在于意识里，而绝不应存在于生命里，——从狂热者那些令人迷醉的结合（他放弃生命的一切杂多，连最纯粹的杂多也放弃——在那种杂多里精神享受自身——并且只意识到上帝，因此只有在死亡中才能消除人格的对立），直到最杂多的意识的现实性，即与世界命运的结合以及上帝对世界命运的对立，——或者是在一切行动和生命表现中感受到的对立，这些行动和表现是以感受自己的受奴役、感受自己那种对立的虚无，来换取自己的正当性的，就像在天主教会里那样；或者是在仅仅或多或少虔诚的思想中上帝的对立，就像在新教教会里那样；——或者是在它的某些教派那里，一个仇恨生命的上帝对生命的对立，被视为耻辱和罪行；或者是一个仁慈的上帝对生命及其欢乐的对立，把一切看作接受来的东西、看作他的恩惠和礼物，看作纯然的现实性，于是那悬浮在现实性之上的精神形态，也在一个神圣的人、先知等等的观念里，被拉低为历史的客观看法——：在这些极端之间，即在对待世界的友好、仇恨或漠不关心这些杂多的或减弱了的意识之间，在这些处于上帝与世界的对立、神圣者与生命的对立之内的极端之间，基督教会向前和向后走完了这个圆圈，但要它在一种非人格的、活生生的美里得到安宁，却是违背它本质品格的；它的命运就是：教会和国家、礼拜和生命、虔诚和美德、教会的作为和世俗的作为，永远不能融而为一。
